Hi everyone,
Recently a new version of he infotainment system FW v70.00.335-C NA was found to have as part of its update process a highly unnecessary, destructive little script called "neutralizeid7" which DIRECTLY TARGETS ITS USERS BY PREFORMING THE UNDESIRABLE ACTION OF REMOVING THE RECOVERY THAT WE USE TO KEEP OUR SYSTEMS OPEN, CUSTOMIZEABLE AND WELL... OURS!!! This incredibly destructive script once again acts kind of like ransomware without the ransom and it wipes out all the recovery files, not that they would work after the update anyways for even the mechanism that would run those files during system boot time is also removed, and just locks you out so completely even connecting to the serial port will no longer work. As of right now, this new FW is only available online for NA region AFAIK and I haven't heard of anyone being updated to it by their dealership yet so even though I am extremely busy these days I took the time to think about how to stay one step ahead and I rewrote the recovery scripts so that the update will think it removed the recovery but really the new recovery slips them right back in there and will even add the required lines of code back to certain files to make the whole thing work again. Early awareness of all this will help minimize the amount of users that loose access to their systems but THIS WILL ONLY WORK IF YOU INSTALL IT BEFORE UPDATING, IF YOU UPDATE TO V70.00.335+ WITHOUT THIS RECOVERY INSTALLED THERE IS NO CHANCE OF EVER TWEAKING YOUR SYSTEM AGAIN, SERIAL CONNECTION WILL NOT EVEN WORK ANYMORE!

So here is the new ID7_V2 recovery but I need a brave soul to test one thing about it. Insofar as the main functionality of these scripts which is to run the tweaks installer for FW v59.00.502+ it works perfectly and exactly the same as the previous id7 recovery. Also, updating to any FW below v70.00.335 will also work as expected but updating to v70.00.335 is right now untested and that is the part I need someone to confirm for me.
So just to reiterate if you want to install this go ahead, it is safe and works exactly like the old version but unless you are that brave tester I am seeking I would wait to update to v70.00.335+ until the test is confirmed. I will update this post after that happens. UPDATE: https://mazda3revolution.com/forums...2018-mazda-3-skyactiv-audio-electronics/234619-id7-recovery-v2.html#post2453907
Happy Hacking My Friends,
~Trez

Dude @Modfreakz, what are you saying? You are the ultimate Guru my friend, you have enlightened me just from our few conversations and built a bench-top CMU for me which led me to better and faster development of AIO than I could have ever imagined and by the way I am forever appreciative of that! But here is the thing, that script deletes the autorun file which we cant really rename but you can regenerate when its missing AND the updated "start_normal_mode.sh" file does not even include the little code snippet that is needed to run autorun in the first place so even when we save autorun and the files they are never even called anymore.
So the last part of my new recovery waits in a loop until it sees that "start_normal_mode.sh" has been created and if ! grep autorun start_normal_mode.sh then it adds the 3 lines back and we are all good. So its a little trickier than just randomizing the file names, you have to do that and rebuild the entire mechanism just like id7 had to rebuild the mechanism that runs the tweaks installer. The major difference here is that this all has to happen during the active update process but thanks to @anderml1955 inadvertently uncovering an astounding secret, our attack surface has an exploit that is so incredibly grand I have to tell you in private because it is truly the ultimate discovery.

@Trezdog44 and @Modfreakz, allow me to throw this out for consideration.

Perhaps you were around when Siutsch’s AIO tweaks were starting up?
There used to be an Easter Egg prior to v56.00.511 that allowed you to go into JCI Test mode, and from there go into option 11 to bring up scripts that I understand became the basis for the AIO package. Two of those scripts allowed you to invoke USB keyboard drivers, followed by a terminal window on the CMU display screen, plugging a keyboard into one of the car’s USB ports, and entering (tweak) commands directly (rather than emulating a terminal via a laptop connected to a serial port):
♦ USB DRIVER → runs usb_drivers.sh : add to kernel all usb drivers (hid, usbhid, sound, midi, audio, keyboard) use before using Terminal

♦ TERMINAL → runs run-terminal.sh : run an in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) Wayland’s Weston terminal with keyboard map defined in /usr/share/wayland/evdev-pc105-us.xkm and accessed by USB keyboard and mouse.

So here is the question: Re 70.00.335+, would this save everyone from having to pull the CMU to hook up via the serial port to emulate a terminal session, by being able to install id7 via USB keyboard/ thumbdrive and the built-in terminal program instead?

I wrote a tweak that adds the Easter Egg back, which can be found here, but one question that comes to mind is whether the USB drivers will play well with the new USB drivers that were introduced in version 59+ firmwares. Sounds like something to explore via benchtesting, now that version 70.00.335+ might require terminal input during installation.

OK everyone here it is https://mazdatweaks.com/id7/, the way to regain access in v70.00.335. It is required to make a serial connection and required to do this immediately after updating BEFORE rebooting. Also, if you have already updated or started with v70.00.335 you can reinstall the same version and do this at the end of the reinstall.
Still working on an automated solution but its little tricky since the update reformats the rootfs then runs only scripts that come packaged in the update. That being said, there is also not much that the developers can do to keep us out of the serial console while the update is running because that is literally the lowest level console and we are tapping straight into it. What I am saying is there is no other way to run the update and we posses the absolute best resource a hacker can possibly have, a physical and direct connection to the system. And why do we have that? Because well... we own it! And if you think about it why would you even need to hack something you own? That is the antithesis of what the free software movement stands for my friends, freedom!

markee89 said:
right click doesn´t work and the combination shift + insert also doesn´t work.
My settings are correct. After the installation was successful the serial connection has been stopped.
Click to expand...
After installation the CMU stops sending information as it is not doing anything and is not running a full Linux system. While the CMU is displaying Reboot..... and the serial data has stopped scrolling press the PC <ENTER> key. If you do not get a # prompt or any response you have something wrong with the serial USB, transmit connection to the CMU or a settings issue in Putty. Check Putty - disconnect the transmit/receive wires from your USB adapter and short the serial adapter transmit/receive wires together, type something on the keyboard and press <ENTER> and see if the information is echoed back to the screen.



ALSO - just because the USB serial adapter transmit light blinks does not mean the data is getting into the CMU - just means the adapter is sending data out the port.

So far I have not tested my complete set of tweaks, but No More Disclaimer Tweak from 2.8.4-1 did not work properly. As requested I sent out the systemApp.js to the email which was mentioned in the tweak install process. Semi-Transparent-Parking-Sensor Tweak from AIO 2.8.4-1 worked fine on FW 70.00.335 EU.

Thanks a lot to @Trezdog44 , @anderml1955 and everyone who contributed to this ID7v2 project!
